narrative:
The model determined that you have a 65% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and the level of savings you currently hold. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single most important reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all or maintain positive balances. This negative status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Your request for credit to buy furniture or equipment also worked against you, although it pulled the prediction slightly toward approval. Most approved customers use loans for radios, televisions, or cars rather than furniture.

Your low savings balance (under 100 DM) further increased the risk score. Nearly half of all applicants have similarly low savings, but this still contributed noticeably toward the bad-credit prediction.

In short, the combination of your overdrawn checking account and limited savings outweighed the modest positive signal from the loan purpose, leading to denial.

To improve your chances next time, focus on clearing your checking account overdraft and building your savings before reapplying. Even modest improvements in those two areas can significantly change how lenders view your application. (218 words)
